description: We are a multidisciplinary team bridging the gap between space exploration and data science. Driven by a passion for human and space exploration—including the Moon, Mars, and Earth orbit—we combine specialized skills in data analysis, management, and visualization with earth science and space weather monitoring. Beyond the numbers, we bring data to life through compelling storytelling, graphic design, and interactive multimedia arts.
summary:
For the 2026 NASA Hackathon challenge, our team built an interactive website that brings the forgotten history of space exploration to life for students and young space fans. Our project features a digital gallery and a built-in 2D game where players can explore the Moon and Mars, walk up to real NASA gear (like Apollo landers, moon mirrors, and Mars rovers), and unlock the stories behind their missions.

What we built: An educational website with an interactive 2D exploration game, a short video demo, and detailed info pages for each piece of space gear.

How it solves the challenge: Instead of forcing kids to read long, boring technical files, our game and website turn real NASA history and science data into a fun, story-driven adventure that grabs their attention.

Why it matters: It connects past space engineering wins with the next generation of explorers, helping students feel a personal connection to the gear left on other worlds and sparking curiosity about the science behind future space missions.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work?

Our project is an interactive website that brings the real equipment NASA left behind on the Moon and Mars back to life. Users visit our site (built on LovableAI) to check out detailed breakdowns of historic space gear, like Apollo landers, mirrors left on the Moon, and Mars rovers.

The Website: An easy-to-read library of space gear with the real stories behind their missions, breaking down complex space history so anyone can understand it.

The 2D Game: Built right into the website is a 2D exploration game. Players drive or walk across the Moon and Mars, find the real artifacts NASA left behind, and click on them to open pop-up cards with real facts, stats, and history.

2. What benefits does it have?

Turns Boring Facts into an Adventure: Instead of reading long, boring textbooks or technical manuals, users learn through a fun game and good storytelling.

Easy for Anyone to Use: Made specifically for students and casual space fans, making space history easy for younger people to understand while keeping all the science accurate.

Keeps People Interested: By mixing active gaming (the 2D game) with regular reading (the info pages), it works well for different types of learners.

3. What is the goal of the project?

Our main goal is to inspire the next generation of scientists, engineers, and astronauts. By sharing the cool engineering stories behind these retired robots and space gear, we want people to feel a real connection to them and get excited about space exploration.

4. What tools, coding, or software did you use?

Website Builder & AI Coding: We used Lovable.ai to quickly turn our research and design ideas into a working website.

Real NASA Data: We gathered and organized real facts, documents, and mission records from NASA about the gear left on the Moon and Mars.

Video & Slides: We made a short video and a pitch presentation to show how the website looks and how the game plays.

5. How is your project creative?

Instead of just making another boring info page or data chart, we mixed learning with casual gaming. Turning real space gear into objects you can actually find in a 2D game lets players "walk" right up to history themselves. It changes the experience from just reading about space to actually exploring it.

6. What things did your team think about while making this?

The Audience: Making sure the words, look, and controls of the game were fun and easy for kids and students to figure out.

Getting the Science Right: Keeping the game fun while making sure every stat, fact, and description of the NASA gear is 100% true.

Smooth Design: Making it super easy to switch between reading the info pages and jumping straight into the 2D game.
